name: NeuroSurge
source_lineage: Based on the 10 November 2026 camera-update preview. Adds display recovery in place of the stop on a refused frame, press-and-drag turning of the brain and mirror body, muscle clicks routed through the existing motor map, paper-ribbon orbit arrows at fixed places, a higher default brain placement, tissue-shaded motor areas, position-welded surface normals, a coordinated forearm and hip turn, a keyboard picture, removal of the floating own-face display, and faster crosshair picking and frame logic. Later the same day: the brain drawn with its real outline (a far-eye picture laid parallel to the screen, straight from above), an ordinary view that draws your own body only in front of your face (the view from behind is unchanged), and a start position of the hand that lets upright windows start. Existing mesh files, asset notices, public provenance redactions and desktop launchers are retained.
anatomy_assets: 490 OBJ meshes retained from the preceding preview. BodyParts3D is CC BY 4.0; Z-Anatomy facial derivatives are CC BY-SA 4.0.
public_preview_authorized: 10 November 2026 user instruction: experimental previews for all projects
browser_verification: Author development checks only: scripted mouse and key input in one desktop Chromium on one pinned processor core, with screenshots, frame-interval counts, the DevTools sampling profiler, a closed-loop sweep of the look and starts at nineteen window sizes, compared against the preceding preview and against this build's previous commit under the same scripts. The latest source commit was also read once by a second instance of the same model, whose six findings were fixed. No independent review yet. Not checked: Firefox, Safari, touch, real phones or tablets, screen readers, reduced-motion settings. This does not establish complete control, timing, joint-mechanics or physiological validation.
known_engineering_gaps: Independent browser review of this build has not been done
Looking around is the slowest path (about 40 frames a second in the author's single-core test, single frames up to about 0.1 s)

The look stops where the whole arm can no longer be shown; on a fast sweep from one look limit to the other the view can be turned a little way back toward the start by itself (it no longer skips frames first)
Key-driven reach is unchanged: already at arm length, whole-hand-in-view and view-edge limits; a wider sweep needs a different hand-anchor design
A clicked muscle switches on a whole motor area and its movement's muscles, not one muscle; some muscles have no movement and only light an area
The leg turn rotates only the hips by 10 degrees; the right upper arm does not turn; hip rotator muscles are not coloured
The left shoulder girdle slides with the arm on both bodies; a slide, not a solved shoulder-blade rotation, and not compared with reference images
The brain's left arrow can sit behind the arm
The brain has its true proportions only at the start look; at a steep look it is stretched like a flat picture

From straight above the lowest lateral areas are hidden: the crosshair reaches 40 of 44 areas without turning the brain (36 with the earlier framing); one arrow click or a short drag brings in the other two on each side, and a status line says so

The ordinary view draws your own body only in front of your face (lap, legs, right forearm and hand, and the whole left arm); the trunk, neck and head are drawn only on the mirror body and in the view from behind; the camera itself did not move

Upright windows start from about 340 by 800 pixels; smaller ones show a message and reload when widened; on phone-sized screens the panels cover much of the brain; touch input is unchanged and unchecked
The retired floating-face code paths remain in the renderer, switched off
SHA256SUMS and release-manifest.json predate these source changes and must be regenerated before release
publication_status: Prepared for review. Not yet published; the release aggregates are stale until regenerated.
